title: 5 Best Keatext Alternatives for Customer Feedback Analytics
summary: The best Keatext alternatives for customer feedback analytics: Thematic, Chattermill, Kapiche, Qualtrics XM Discover, Medallia. Where each one wins.
body_markdown:
Most teams looking for Keatext alternatives aren't unhappy with the analysis. They've outgrown the shape of it. Keatext scopes and prices its plans by how many records you analyze in a year. Its published tiers top out starting at 30,000 records annually. Enterprise feedback programs run an order of magnitude past that in a single channel.


The best Keatext alternative for enterprise customer feedback analytics is Thematic, when the priority is analyzing feedback at enterprise volume and quantifying[which themes moved a score](https://getthematic.com/insights/quantify-themes-moved-nps-score) . Thematic builds a[two-level theme taxonomy](https://getthematic.com/insights/ai-powered-customer-feedback-theme-discovery) from the feedback itself rather than from a template. It links each theme to its[measured impact](https://getthematic.com/insights/link-feedback-themes-nps-csat-drivers) on net promoter score (NPS) or customer satisfaction score (CSAT). Every theme traces back to the raw comments behind it, so a skeptical executive can interrogate the number instead of taking it on faith.


Other tools fit other situations. Chattermill suits high-volume feedback across many languages and business units. Kapiche suits mid-market insights teams that want a fast first result on survey data. Qualtrics XM Discover suits enterprises already committed to Qualtrics. Medallia suits organizations that want text analytics inside a broad experience suite.


This list compares each tool on the two things that actually decide a Keatext replacement: how much feedback it can take, and how many kinds. Tools that only collect feedback were cut, because Keatext doesn't collect either. Below is the shortlist, why teams move, where each option genuinely wins, and what to ask before signing anything.


## The list at a glance


1. **Thematic** : enterprise customer experience (CX) and insights teams that need traceable themes and quantified score impact at high volume.
2. **Chattermill** : large CX-led brands analyzing high-volume feedback across many languages and business units.
3. **Kapiche** : mid-market insights teams that want fast topic discovery on survey feedback without building a code frame.
4. **Qualtrics XM Discover** : enterprises already running Qualtrics that need omnichannel conversational analytics.
5. **Medallia** : organizations that want text analytics and impact scoring inside a broad experience management suite.


Here is the same shortlist side by side, with Keatext as the baseline.


Tool Best for Main trade-off


Keatext Small to mid annual record volumes across reviews, surveys, and Zendesk tickets Published plans scope by annual records, with the top tier starting at 30,000+


Thematic Enterprise CX and insights teams needing traceable themes and quantified score movement Analyzes feedback but does not collect it


Chattermill High-volume, multilingual feedback across many business units Strong on analysis, lighter on driving the next action


Kapiche Mid-market insights teams wanting a fast first result Per-project row limits; narrower integrations at scale


Qualtrics XM Discover Enterprises already on Qualtrics needing conversational analytics Reported six-figure annual add-on cost; taxonomy setup needs specialists


Medallia Organizations wanting text analytics inside a broad experience suite Setup and ongoing taxonomy management take real internal resource


## Why teams look past Keatext


Keatext is an AI-based text analytics platform that describes itself as delivering "a unified view of your unstructured customer feedback." It syncs from surveys, public reviews, and support tickets, with a named deep integration for Zendesk. Its Focus Recommendations feature surfaces what it identifies as key drivers of customer satisfaction. It's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) compliant and[SOC 2](https://www.aicpa-cima.com/resources/landing/system-and-organization-controls-soc-suite-of-services) certified. In December 2024 it announced[a partnership with QuestionPro](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2024/12/11/2995335/0/en/Keatext-and-QuestionPro-Partner-to-Expand-Conversational-Analytics-and-Unify-Insights.html) that lets QuestionPro customers pull surveys, reviews, support tickets, and contact center transcripts into one analysis.


For a team analyzing review sites and a Zendesk queue, that's a reasonable fit. Unlike most of the alternatives below, Keatext publishes its list pricing openly. The friction shows up in two places.


**Annual record volume.** Keatext's published plans are scoped by[records analyzed per year](https://www.keatext.ai/en/pricing/) : 10,000 on Basic, 20,000 on Pro, and 30,000+ on Enterprise. Mitre 10, New Zealand's largest home improvement retailer, processes about 20,000 verbatim comments a month across 84 stores with a three-person insights team. Units differ between vendors, so confirm how a record gets counted. The order of magnitude is the point: one retailer's monthly volume is the size of a full annual plan.


**Source breadth.** Reviews, surveys, and tickets are three of the channels an enterprise CX program runs. Call transcripts, in-product feedback, complaints logs, social, and customer relationship management (CRM) notes are the rest.[Stitching them into one view](https://getthematic.com/insights/integrate-feedback-sources-analytics-platform) is where the enterprise version of this problem lives. Keatext charges separately for wider collection: data acquisition from 100+ review sites and additional data connectors are both add-ons.


Neither is a flaw. They're a scope decision. The question is whether your program sits inside that scope or outside it.


## 1. Thematic


**Thematic** is the customer intelligence layer for enterprise CX, insights, and product teams that have to defend their themes to someone who will push back. It analyzes unstructured feedback from surveys, support tickets, call transcripts, app reviews, and social. It sits on top of the existing stack rather than replacing it.


The difference from Keatext is what Thematic does with a theme once it has found one. Thematic builds the taxonomy bottom-up, so the structure emerges from the feedback rather than from categories written two years ago. There's no rebuild cycle when customers change how they talk. Analysts can inspect, merge, split, and edit that structure directly. Thematic quantifies each theme's impact on NPS or CSAT, and separately reports score change across two periods. So a team reports "delivery delays cost 5 points, support improvements gained 4" instead of "NPS dropped 3 points." Every theme clicks through to the raw comments underneath it.


The proof is in enterprise throughput. DoorDash analyzed tens of thousands of NPS survey responses from consumers, merchants, and delivery drivers with Thematic, and surfaced "Merchant Frustration" as a hidden driver of declining NPS. The root cause was a Menu Manager tool that took 11 seconds to load each edit. After the redesign, load times dropped to under 3 seconds. Mitre 10 runs about 20,000 verbatim comments a month across 84 stores with a three-person insights team, and quantified stock availability as half an NPS point of impact. Forrester Consulting, in a[Total Economic Impact study](https://getthematic.com/forrester-total-economic-impact-study) commissioned by Thematic, measured a 543% three-year return on investment with payback in under six months.


**The trade-off.** Thematic doesn't collect feedback. It analyzes what you already collect, wherever you collect it. If you need one vendor to send the survey and analyze the responses, Thematic is half the answer and Medallia or Qualtrics is the other half.


## 2. Chattermill


**Chattermill** is the strongest fit for large, CX-led enterprises processing high volumes of feedback across many languages and business units. It unifies surveys, reviews, social, support conversations, and voice, then applies deep-learning aspect-based sentiment analysis to surface the drivers behind an experience.


Chattermill analyzes feedback in more than 100 languages, with automated translation and transcription built in. It connects with more than 65 feedback channels. It carries SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001:2022. If you're leaving Keatext over language coverage or channel count, this is the most direct step up.


**The trade-off.** Chattermill is analytics-oriented by design. It's strong at telling a team what's trending and weaker at driving the next action, so it surfaces the theme without filing the ticket. Pricing is custom and quoted after a sales conversation, which is a step back from Keatext's published tiers if budget predictability was part of the appeal.


## 3. Kapiche


**Kapiche** fits mid-market and enterprise insights teams that want fast topic discovery on survey and conversation feedback. It's the closest like-for-like replacement for Keatext, and often the right call for a team that wants a lateral move rather than an enterprise step up.


Kapiche applies natural language processing with no manual code-frame setup, then layers on sentiment, topic clustering, taxonomy classification, and predictive signals such as churn and escalation forecasting. The appeal is speed to a first useful result, which is the same appeal Keatext trades on.


**The trade-off.** Scale, in the same shape as the problem you're leaving. Kapiche prices per project, with row limits running from 50,000 to 250,000 by tier. Its Bronze tier starts at $1,060 per month. That's a higher ceiling than Keatext's published tiers, but it's still a ceiling. Its integration ecosystem is also narrower than the enterprise incumbents. If you're moving because you hit a volume wall, check the new wall before you sign.


## 4. Qualtrics XM Discover


**Qualtrics XM Discover** is the natural choice for enterprises already running Qualtrics that need omnichannel conversational analytics. Formerly Clarabridge, it analyzes feedback across cases, chat, voice transcriptions, email, surveys, and third-party reviews. It uses natural language understanding to extract intent, emotion, effort, and sentiment.


Where it wins is contact-center-grade analysis at scale inside an established Qualtrics program. If the contact center is the reason you outgrew Keatext, and Qualtrics is already your survey platform, this is the shortest path.


**The trade-off.** Cost and complexity, both a long way from Keatext's published list prices. XM Discover is reported to run as a $300,000 to $400,000 per year add-on, on top of a base platform starting around $25,000 per year. Taxonomy setup in Designer needs specialists and ongoing maintenance. Teams moving off a lightweight tool find this a big step up in both spend and admin overhead.


## 5. Medallia


**Medallia** suits organizations that want text analytics sitting inside a broad experience management suite rather than as a separate layer. Its in-platform text analytics parses verbatims at the phrase level, sorts them into topic hierarchies, and applies sentiment. It also offers impact scoring that shows how topics move NPS up or down.


The breadth is real. Collection, analysis, and program management sit in one place, which is the argument for consolidating rather than adding another point tool alongside your survey platform.


**The trade-off.** Weight. Setup and ongoing taxonomy management take real internal time. A team that liked Keatext for its short setup should scope that carefully before committing.


## How to choose between them


The right pick depends on what broke first. Ask these during a demo, and insist on seeing each one run against your own feedback.


- **What's the volume limit, and is it counted in records, rows, or comments?** Get the number in the unit your program reports in. A vague answer usually means the limit is real and negotiable. That's fine, as long as it's priced before you sign.
- **Which of our sources can you take today, without an add-on?** List your channels first, then ask. Reviews and tickets are the easy ones. Call transcripts, in-product feedback, and CRM notes are where the gaps show up.
- **Can we see and edit the theme taxonomy?** A good answer shows you the themes, lets you merge or split them, and traces each back to the underlying comments. A vague answer means a black box.
- **Can it tell us which themes moved the score, not just which are most common?** Ask for a score change breakdown across two periods. Frequency without impact sends teams to fix the loudest complaint rather than the costliest one.
- **How long until the first reliable report?** Hours or days is strong. Weeks of model training or code-frame setup is a heavier lift than a Keatext replacement warrants.
- **What does it cost at our volume, all in?** Include setup, professional services, connectors, and any per-source collection fees. Keatext's published pricing gives you a baseline to compare against. Most of the alternatives will quote.


## The short version


For most teams leaving Keatext because their feedback volume or channel count outgrew the plan, Thematic is the strongest alternative: themes built bottom-up from your own data, quantified impact on the score, and every theme traceable to the comments behind it.


Chattermill is the runner-up for high-volume multilingual programs. Kapiche is the better call for a mid-market team that wants a lateral move rather than an enterprise platform. If the contact center is the driver and you already run Qualtrics, look at XM Discover first.


The fastest way to decide is to run the same batch of your own feedback through your top two, then ask each vendor to show you exactly how one theme was built and how much of the last score change it explains. If you can defend the number to your CFO, you've found your tool.


If your shortlist reaches past this page, Thematic compares the field against other incumbents in its guides to[Chattermill alternatives](https://getthematic.com/insights/chattermill-alternatives-and-competitors) ,[Qualtrics alternatives](https://getthematic.com/insights/qualtrics-competitors-and-alternatives) , and[Medallia alternatives](https://getthematic.com/insights/top-medallia-alternatives) .
